title: Hybrid-functional exact-exchange electronic-iteration cost transition

input_tags.name: LHFCALC
input_tags.role: Selects Hartree-Fock/DFT hybrid functional type calculations.

input_tags.name: NELMDL
values: default -5 in common no-WAVECAR starts unless another default or explicit value applies
input_tags.role: Controls initial non-self-consistent delay steps with fixed Hamiltonian.

contextual_statement: VASP hybrid-functional and HF-type calculations include nonlocal Hartree-Fock exchange, whose evaluation can be much more expensive than semilocal DFT. In starts where NELMDL applies, VASP may first perform non-self-consistent blocked-Davidson delay steps with a fixed Hamiltonian; for HF-type calculations with NELMDL >= 3, these delay steps use the corresponding semilocal local Hamiltonian. When the calculation leaves that delay and begins evaluating the hybrid/HF exact-exchange workload, the wall time per electronic step can increase dramatically.
diagnostic_relevance: For an applicable VASP hybrid-functional calculation, a small number of quick initial DAV-labelled electronic iterations followed by a much longer next electronic step is consistent with the expected onset of expensive exact-exchange work. That pattern alone is not evidence that VASP is hung, that electronic convergence failed, or that HSE06 is incompatible with SOC. It also does not rule out a real performance or execution problem; other evidence such as scheduler termination, lack of output over the available wall time, resource limits, logs, and convergence history must still be assessed separately.

shorthand_correction.shorthand: HSE starts at the fifth step
shorthand_correction.correction: This is an oversimplification. The visible transition can occur around the fifth electronic iteration in common from-scratch starts where the effective NELMDL delay is -5 and no WAVECAR is present, but the exact iteration depends on NELMDL, ISTART/WAVECAR state, INIWAV/IALGO defaults, VASP version and settings, and the selected electronic algorithm.

limitations: This record supplies contextual reference evidence only; it does not diagnose any specific VASP run.

The directly matching VASP Forum example discusses HSE06 with ALGO=Normal; applicability to ALGO=Damped is supported through VASP Wiki documentation of NELMDL delay behavior and HF/hybrid algorithm recommendations, not through that forum example alone.
The step number is not unconditional. Explicit NELMDL, a present WAVECAR, different start settings, or different algorithms can change the number and character of initial delay steps.

Large wall time in an electronic step can still reflect an execution, scaling, resource, or convergence problem. This context only prevents premature interpretation of the transition as a hang or HSE06/SOC incompatibility by itself.
Cost and scaling depend on system size, k-point sampling, number of bands, exact-exchange workload, precision settings, VASP version, and parallelization choices such as NCORE and KPAR.
This record does not recommend changing INCAR tags, k-point meshes, NCORE, KPAR, NKRED, SOC, or functional choices.

sources.title: HSE06 calculation stuck at 5th electronic step.
sources.applicability_note: A VASP forum moderator explains a directly relevant HSE06 case: initial steps were quick because they were non-self-consistent with no Hamiltonian update, followed by much higher effort when exact exchange had to be computed. The example specifically refers to ALGO=Normal.
